title: Comparative Assessment of Readability Using RTI and VRTI
author: Luisa Ammirati

steps.title: Recruit participants
steps.instruction: Recruit at least 30 participants who have a homogeneous background in paleontology (e.g., fourth‑year geology students).

steps.title: Set up experimental environment
steps.instruction: Arrange a large room divided into two distinct sections, one for the RTI group and one for the VRTI group. In each section place two seating stations: Station A equipped with two Android tablets and Station B equipped with two iPads and Apple Pencils. Ensure the session is conducted simultaneously for both groups in a controlled setting (e.g., during class) so that participants start at Station A and then proceed to Station B.

substeps.instruction: Material required: 2 Android tablets for Station A; 2 iPads with 2 Apple Pencils for Station B; Adobe Photoshop 2020.

steps.title: Prepare media and workspace
steps.instruction: Capture two snapshots of the RTI and VRTI footprint surveys using the RTI viewer. Spatially align the two images to achieve pixel‑level correspondence and place the aligned pair onto a neutral background in Adobe Photoshop. Create a pre‑configured Photoshop workspace where the footprint image is set as a locked background layer.

substeps.instruction: Open the RTI snapshot in Photoshop and have a domain expert draw two separate layers (3 px brush): perimeter of the footprint in green (RGB 0, 255, 0) and the second‑finger digit pad in yellow (RGB 255, 255, 0) to serve as ground‑truth annotations.

steps.title: Configure devices at stations
steps.instruction: Load the appropriate files on each tablet/iPad for the upcoming annotation task.

substeps.instruction: Station A – Tablet 1: open the RTI file in the RTI viewer (Relight 2026.01, https://github.com/cnr-isti-vclab/relight/releases).
Station A – Tablet 2: open the VRTI file in the RTI viewer.
Station B – iPad 1: open the Photoshop workspace containing the RTI footprint.
Station B – iPad 2: open the Photoshop workspace containing the VRTI footprint.

steps.title: Create participant annotation layers
steps.instruction: In each iPad workspace, for every participant n, create two transparent layers named "Student n (a)" and "Student n (b)".

steps.title: Set brush size and colors
steps.instruction: Set the brush size to 3 px. Assign colors based on layer label: all layers ending with “(a)” receive green (RGB 0, 255, 0); all layers ending with “(b)” receive yellow (RGB 255, 255, 0).

steps.title: Demonstrate expected annotation
steps.instruction: Show participants an example of the expected result on a separate footprint, illustrating both a perimeter annotation and a digit‑pad detail annotation.

steps.title: Instruct participants to annotate
steps.instruction: For each participant, ask them to:

substeps.instruction: Trace the footprint perimeter on layer "Student n (a)" using the green color (RGB 0, 255, 0) with a 3 px stroke.
Mark the digit pad of the second finger on layer "Student n (b)" using the yellow color (RGB 255, 255, 0) with a 3 px stroke.
Maintain consistent thickness and colour throughout the experiment and annotate only features they consider reliable; the perimeter may be an open contour.

steps.title: Adjust lighting and capture screenshot
steps.instruction: Each participant explores the RTI viewer on the tablet assigned to their group (RTI group on RTI footprint, VRTI group on VRTI footprint) and adjusts the light direction to a condition they deem optimal for morphological interpretation. Then capture a screenshot of that lighting condition.

steps.title: Export annotation layers as PNGs
steps.instruction: Open the completed Photoshop file containing all participant annotations. For each layer:

substeps.instruction: Make only the target layer visible.
Export the layer as an individual .png file, preserving the original image resolution.
Ensure the exported file retains a transparent or neutral background.

steps.title: Organize exported files
